The shaytaan will say to the man: «You are not going to accept this from the woman». And the reverse: «You are not going to accept this from your husband. Say that to your wife, say that to your husband». Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa knows that the shaytaan will play a game here.
And that is why Allaah has made a solution. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa warns us against the shaytaan. He makes clear to us what the solution against the shaytaan and the djinn (spirits) is: that you say «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم» — «I seek refuge with Allaah from the accursed shaytaan». When someone wants to advise the other, that he begins by advising the other and performs the isti3aadhah (seeking refuge with Allaah) by saying to him: «Before we continue, say: ‹I seek refuge with Allaah from the accursed shaytaan›» or by reciting aayat al-Kursie (the verse of the Throne). This isti3aadhah is an important matter with which you must begin your communication when you have made a bad utterance or another has made a bad utterance. Then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says that He is As-Samie3 (the All-Hearing) over what we do and say, and that He is Al-3Aliem (the All-Knowing) of our hearts, that is: of the intentions with which we utter that. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa makes clear in these verses which medicine you can use, what the origin of that medicine is, and what the method of the medicine is.
Before you speak, it is important that you set the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [as a goal]. You must be patient with what you say and say the best. The origin of the medicine in good speech [is] patience, and the medicine itself when speaking [is] that you have the best utterances. And in order to swallow such a medicine in the correct manner, you must perform the isti3aadhah. And even if you had no whisperings, you must perform the isti3aadhah in order to repel the whisperings.
And an example of this is that you say to your husband: «May Allaah be pleased with you, may Allaah watch over you, I very much want to please you, I want Allaah to guard us». We have explained before that good communication entails that one listens to the other, opens up, communicates without judgement. That was when we dealt with accepting advice [the nasiehah]. Then we also dealt with giving advice. Accepting advice must be paired with a sincere intention when listening. And among the important matters in this is that we read that lesson once more and try to realise it.
When listening, it is very important that you make yourself aware of the position you are in and with which you must listen; because listening relates to the position with which you listen: are you a pupil or a teacher? Are you someone with authority or someone over whom there is authority? Are you the one who leads or the one who is led? Both make a difference in listening. The problem of many men and women is that they listen from an incorrect position. And it is important that you listen to one another from a correct position. With the two partners, they must listen according to the task that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has designated for them. The man is the educator of his wife and listens from that position. And he must also listen from the position of the husband.
Listening from the position of the educator — [there is] a difference between the educator (the teacher, the man, or the husband). When the man listens, he must listen with all his tasks, taking all his tasks into account. He is a man who educates and he must be loving. He is not a father and not a teacher, and also not an employer. He is a man who must be loving and must be an educator for his wife. From these tasks the man must listen. So that means that he must listen in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and with an ear with which he picks up the signals in order to know how his wife thinks and how his wife feels, so that he can improve her thinking and her feeling, and so that he can afterwards carry out his task as an educator, and also [his task] as a loving partner with which he seeks closeness to her in order to draw near to her heart, so that the tarbiyah becomes easier.
And the woman must therefore listen from her position as a humble, compliant woman, who is being educated, who must learn from her husband, or [who] seeks solutions, or [who] seeks how she can please her husband, how she can complete her husband, how she can support his leadership and not oppose it. From this task and this position the woman must listen, and even if injustice is done to her, she must advise him from her position. She makes sure that she wins her husband's heart and then utters good words. And that is among the important matters that also belong to repelling the evil with the better. That you also think: from which position should I listen, and how should I influence my husband in the correct manner? The position of the man and the woman also suits our fitrah (natural disposition). You must listen and speak from that position.
How do you know in what manner someone has listened to you? You can — usually — also see that from how he spoke. When he has listened with the ear of a teacher, he will speak as a teacher. When the woman listens from the position [that] she has the say [the upper hand], then that will also be clear from her words and the manner in which she places her words and assumes her posture while she speaks.
Listening also has an effect on the response [the reaction]. In some people the fitrah is broken, whereby the position of the other is taken. When that happens, conflicts will arise.
The ustaadh (teacher) once met a man who said in the presence of the wife: «You did not tell me anything; if you had said so, I would have done it» (meaning that she should have commanded him). Or that man [said]: «I do not know how you want our child to be treated at that moment; if you say so, I will do it». At that moment you, as a man, are not listening, but as if you were a woman. And the woman at that moment is not listening as a woman but as a man, and then great conflicts arise. Because the children will then not listen as children but as equals. When the man takes the position of the woman, he will not show leadership and will not educate, and then the tarbiyah of his wife disappears and the tarbiyah of his children disappears; because he sees himself as equal to them.
For example, [a woman] says: «Yes, but if you ask him something and he does not do it, you will go and hit him. Yes, but if I do what he says, then I also have to do what he says». Or [a man] says: «Yes, but he must obey me. My child must obey me, but I have never treated him the way he treats me now». Allaahu l-musta3aan (Allaah is the One Whose help is sought). You in reality [think] that he is unjust [because] you did not treat him the way he treats you now, so you [thereby] place him as an equal, and then tarbiyah is no longer possible. When you listen and behave as a person equal to another, then the other will also treat you in that manner.
The man who does not educate [is] — for example — a man whose wife is angry with him and mocks him with ridicule or sarcasm, whereupon the man picks that up and does the same thing. So you sometimes literally see spouses treating each other like small children. They go and imitate each other in a mocking manner. Then you are no longer an educator as a man, but [you are] small children hurting each other. And this ensures that more conflicts come and arise, that no solutions are used, and that the woman values her husband's position less. You see that there is not a single grain of respect between the two of them. The man must be above this behaviour and perform the isti3aadhah. And the woman must also perform the isti3aadhah and calm down. The man must remind the woman of the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
With many people, «the honour [the pride]» stands in the way, that is, the self [the ego]. One must first concern oneself with the right of Allaah. In the end you want, together, to preserve the marriage and work for the pleasure of Allaah. If everyone drags in his honour («my honour has been wounded, my ego has been touched, that is [that] my arrogance has entered the arena»), then the solution is impossible. For then the gaps will grow larger and the man will no longer be able to find a solution.
So it is important — instead of basing yourself on a supposed ego or honour — that you base yourself on the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. The man must utter his words in a loving manner by saying — for example —: «My dear wife, may Allaah forgive you, I do not want you to fall into sins». [There are] of course many other beautiful words that can be said. The matter [concerns] the essence of the words, not literally these words. This attitude is different from going along with the woman's anger: «No, you are such and such, look at yourself, no, you certainly do [it] better». Then there is no tarbiyah.
The partners complete one another, and they must remove the evil from one another by means of the better. If the man — for example — insults the woman or accuses her of something, then she performs the isti3aadhah, asks her husband to also perform the isti3aadhah, and then makes sure that she utters the best words towards her husband in order to calm him. By saying — for example —: «My dear husband, sit down. I will do what you say» or «My dear husband, you are everything to me. Instruct me and I will go and do what you say» or simply by doing what he says if you know what he wants, or by calming him in another way.
Make sure that at that moment you do not go and hold a discussion with him, but that you go and obey him; do not go into a dispute at that moment and do not ask questions. That you must not do. Only hold a conversation when you have both calmed down and the shaytaan has been removed at that moment. Only then do you hold a conversation.
Questions
Question: We are not held to account as long as we do not utter anything. How is it then when you have certain thoughts and you discuss them? For example, someone who doubts the religion.
The answer: At that moment you must perform the isti3aadhah, change your posture, and say «I believe in Allaah and His messengers», and you must not utter it.
The sister: So you cannot — if [the matter] lasts long — present it to someone.
The ustaadh: If [the matter] is resolved by this, then you should not present it. And if [the doubts] are real, then you must present them — yes — to someone with knowledge, not to anyone else.
The sister: Sometimes the people in her environment say [that] certain thoughts come to someone, and then they say it in a manner that makes them afraid [become fearful of it].
The ustaadh: You must advise them to perform the isti3aadhah, and to perform the istighfaar (asking for forgiveness). And if [the matter] is really a doubt and has become a thought, then they must present it only to people with knowledge.
Question: I was recently told that it [is] makroeh (disliked) to pray with Soerat Al-Masad. Is that correct? It was a sister who told her that. She said that the evidence [is] that in Soerat Al-Masad the position of Aboe Lahab is mentioned.
The ustaadh: As long as we have not heard a hadieth or a statement of a sahaabie (companion), this statement does not exist with us. And that [is] the manner in which we must deal with this matter. You must say to that [person]: «You must not spread the matter as long as there are no evidences». And it may be that that [person] himself — although he spreads the evil and does not bring it out — does not like it being spoken about, or does not find it pleasant that Aboe Lahab is spoken about, or does not want the Fire to be spoken about. The answer for that sister: if you have no evidences, then it is not permissible for you to speak on the matter, and it is also not permissible for you to say that you think so, for people can be influenced by this. Conjecture is not evidence.
The tafsier (explanation) of Soerat Al-A3laa. In it [it is mentioned] that a group of people [say] that Soerat Al-Masad may not be used, but that is refuted therein. The evidence for its permissibility is that there is no evidence for its impermissibility. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa does not dislike a matter He has brought. How can Allaah utter matters that He afterwards dislikes?
Another sister wanted to make use [of the matter with her question]; because she was at that gathering. [The sister] heard that it caused confusion for the sisters who were with her when [the sister] raised [that statement]. How can we — in the best way — deal with this in a group of sisters [who] also have less knowledge? It even got to the point that a sister said: «So I put effort into learning Soerat Al-Masad for nothing». How should we deal with this?
These are students of two sisters under the supervision of their two teachers. They give tadjwied lessons (lessons in correct Qur-aan recitation). Questions of Islamic knowledge they present to the ustaadh. Some of them are practising, some not at all, some are learning a few soewar [chapters of the Qur-aan]. One of the students said that in the group and it truly caused confusion.
The ustaadh: Then you must also explain this rule clearly to everyone: «O noble, honourable sisters, we know that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given us our religion, which we learn through the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. We must not take [adopt] that when people say something without evidence. And the statement without evidence is not a correct statement».
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam spoke in a hadieth narrated by 3Aa-ishah. 3Aa-ishah asks: «O Messenger of Allaah, who [has] the greatest right over the woman?». He said: «Her husband». And in another hadieth the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says to a woman: «انظُري أين أنتِ منه، فإنه جنّتُك ونارُك» — «Look at where you stand with him, for he is your Paradise and your Fire», that is: what he sees [believes] concerning you. That is why the ustaadh kept insisting on the pleasure. This hadieth has been declared hasan (good) by Imaam al-Albaanie.
The homework
At least two hours spent organising the notes, reading them and absorbing them well. At least two hours.
Practising the points we discussed in the lesson, and for the sisters who received a correction with regard to their previous homework: that they practise it in a better way according to the correction they received.
We are now in the process of improving ourselves towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and learning certain habits. And these new habits need time. When we do not train ourselves repeatedly, it will be difficult to hold on to these matters — in the end — as well. And that is why we will do our homework in this manner — in shaa Allaah (if Allaah wills) — in the coming weeks.
Lesson forty — Sunday 9 December 2018
The homework (2 December)
At least two hours spent organising the notes, reading them and absorbing them well. At least two hours.
Practising the points we discussed in the lesson, and for the sisters who received a correction with regard to their previous homework: that they practise it in a better way according to the correction they received.
We are now in the process of improving ourselves towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and accustoming ourselves to certain matters. These new habits need time. So if we do not train ourselves in them repeatedly, it will in the end be difficult to commit to these matters. And that is why we will — in this manner — do our homework — in shaa Allaah — also in the coming weeks.
Discussion of the homework (9 December)
Experience of student 1
The sister also occupied herself with the homework of the past weeks because it coincides. Especially the sentence that we should utter before our partners or our parents: «I want you to be pleased with me, in order to thereby please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa». The sister occupied herself with this a lot, but in a different way. It was difficult for the sister to utter this in that way without giving an explanation. For she is gathering a lot of information about the position of the parents in Islaam, in order to give it to them, and to let them know what their position is, and that she wants to please them for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and so that they are aware of what they represent to her, and that the sister wants them to be pleased with her so that Allaah will be pleased.
The ustaadh: I would connect the first point to Tawhied (the Oneness of Allaah). Everything good that you want to show to a non-Muslim, it is important that you connect it to Tawhied. And you do that by making clear that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has created us, and that He knows us best. According to the starting point or the background of the person concerned whom you want to invite. If that person's background is atheism, then make clear to him that this is a proof of the existence of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, then make clear that Allaah knows the people best, then acquaint him with Islaam, then invite him to Islaam. And if he is a Christian or a Jew, then it is important that you base [the speech] on the foundation he has, that is, you proceed from the fact that he acknowledges a god, but that he commits shirk (associating partners with Allaah). Then you see that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. That is how you connect that [person] to Tawhied, and not that [the matter] is merely a question of beautiful symbolic ethics.
The sister: Then she started on the [other] points. In preparation [for the matter], she revised a lot in order to absorb it and be able to practise it in daily life, such as «be positive and persevere», «avoid the negativities in your life». The sister noticed that she quickly allows negative thoughts into her head. She allows negative thoughts about herself, such as that she did not do [something] in a good way, or that things sometimes do not go as she wants, and this is not correct thinking. And it is important that she is aware of that and is more flexible, because she wants to hold on more than necessary to an image she has drawn for herself. And in reality [it] does not have to go that way.
The ustaadh: How can you get out of the negativity?
The sister: What helps her when there is something of negativity is to think calmly and say: al-hamdu-li-llaah (all praise is due to Allaah), everything is a blessing from Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And this is something she should be more aware of. Something in which you do not see the good at that moment, [know] that that too is a blessing from Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. So very simply: al-hamdu-li-llaah, al-hamdu-li-llaah, al-hamdu-li-llaah. And focusing on what is good. For example, when she has to give a presentation, she does not memorise something as quickly as she would like, or she had not arranged something as neatly as she would like, or when giving the presentation she forgets to mention something, and does not know how to deal with it; then negativity may start up in her head even though the matter is perhaps not like that at all. And with a positive outlook [the matter] can be solved well, especially with such examples. Perhaps she forgot something, but al-hamdu-li-llaah, the message got through, and that is what matters. And if she forgot something, she can — nevertheless — still mention it during [the talk], for example.
The ustaadh: How you handle this very simply — this is a very simple matter. Actually [these are] matters we should accustom ourselves to well. We always return to the foundation, and the foundation of everything is that we have ikhlaas. If we have ikhlaas, then that [is] the processing system. You seek the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. If you do the utmost you can at that moment, then you are seeking the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. If [the matter] does not work out one hundred percent for you and you go and repeat, should you panic or be glad? You are glad.
The sister: Merely the fact that you do this and try, you have — in shaa Allaah — already achieved it in advance.
The ustaadh: You should then be glad, because every time you try, you receive more reward. For what do you do it? To receive the reward of Allaah. And every time you try again, you receive hasanaat (good deeds/rewards) — in shaa Allaah — if you intend that in the correct way. We are here to gather hasanaat, not to give a presentation. And that gives you much more peace. No frustration, and steadfastness. If you made a mistake and thought: did I do this in a good manner or not, [know] that you did your best; as long as you do not utter wrong things that anger Allaah, you have reached your goal. And that makes [it so] that when you go and examine yourself and improve and correct yourself, you do so for the sake of Allaah, not for the sake of the people, or because it has to look so professional. For that is a form of delusion. And that is something that can divert that [person] from ikhlaas. One focuses on professionalism and [superficial] perfection, while he is not occupied with ikhlaas. How can you combine these two matters: by using these things to please Allaah. For example, you use professionalism as a means to perfect your affair for the sake of Allaah, as long as «for the sake of Allaah» remains in it and is not merely a background thought. It must become your goal. And to this we must accustom ourselves: I want only the reward, and I focus on the reward of Allaah.
If you focus on [the matter:] it is not professional, it is not as perfect as I want. Perfection [is] that you do it for the sake of Allaah, not that you make no mistakes, for everyone makes mistakes. And part of the perfection of man is that he is not perfect. Therefore one must focus on the goal: the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Experience of student 2
As for the homework, the points she practised this week [are] paying attention to the words she utters, being aware of what she says. For she often has [the tendency], when she is in a conversation or when she is telling something, not to weigh her words well. She paid attention to that, especially towards her mother. A situation occurred in which she could not judge well how she should respond to the situation. Before that, [she had] this week once again failed at judging well and using the right words towards her mother.
The ustaadh: As long as you try for the sake of Allaah, you have not failed. You must try time and time again. The feeling of failure is a feeling that our desire [our soul that commands evil] instils in us so that it does not let us try: «You were not made for this, continue your life as you always continue», and that is a danger. We must not fall into it. As long as we keep trying, we have reward. And if you stop trying, we are not only without reward, but sins rest upon us.
Perhaps you can present it.
The sister: It was a situation in which her mother said something at which the sister thought: does she really mean this? The mother said: «I will not go, I was not invited», while she is invited. Her mother does not have WhatsApp. She [the sister] invited her; I was with her. The mother had a feeling that she was not really welcome. She said: «No, I will not go». So when the sister tried to convince her to go, her mother became very angry. The sister did not know whether she should go along with her [in the conversation] or continue convincing.
The ustaadh: How is your relationship with the one who invited you?
The sister: She is my aunt.
The ustaadh: At that moment you had a feeling [for the feelings] of your mother. Your mother has something [occupying her]. At that moment you call your aunt and say: «Would you not like to make your sister happy for the sake of Allaah? Can you call my mother separately to invite her?».
The sister: She did call her, but [that] was a few weeks ago.
The ustaadh: Then let her call her again.
The sister: She is afraid that she will think strangely of her mother.
The ustaadh: You approach the matter from a different angle. Your approach to it is wrong if you were to say: «My mother is angry».
The sister: The aunt is older than her mother.
The ustaadh: Then you say to her: «Your younger sister will be very happy if her older sister confirms it to her by calling». And among the best deeds with Allaah is bringing joy to another. What she thinks or does not think is a matter that concerns her. Your task is not to let her think this. Moreover, at that moment you could also have called [someone who advises you] as to what you could do in the best way. There should be more of this [it should increase]. Should I encourage her to go anyway or not? And among the things with which you could have encouraged her is to say: «She is your older sister, so Allaah will make you happy if you go. You are invited, so if you go there you will make her very happy, and she is your older sister». Every opportunity you can benefit from, you should take.
The sister: The sister was hesitant about urging her to go, so she became even angrier.
The ustaadh: If you go pushing [forcefully], that [person] thinks his feeling is being ignored. You can change that feeling with another thought. By redirecting the thought to focus on her heart and the heart of the sister. Then you are occupied with the thought. If the thought changes and the place of its focus changes, the feeling also changes, and with it the action changes.
Experience of student 3
«I paid attention this past week to my communication with my husband, and I noticed that I do not always show humility. I have become more aware of this, and I forced myself daily to reflect on the words I utter in general, and especially towards my husband.
I have started listening more according to my task. I noticed what my husband finds pleasant, and what he loves, and what he does not find pleasant, and what he does not love.
I had a bad habit, namely that I was sometimes still busy with my phone while my husband was speaking to me. This habit I no longer do.»
The ustaadh: Every time, be aware of ikhlaas so that [the matter] continues. The phone you only pick up when you think it is something important. Smartphones are the fitnah (trial) of this time. If there is something very important, only then do you look. It is important to give up Facebook, and to give up all kinds of social media (which are means of [foolish] triviality), except WhatsApp and the phone. You do not need Facebook or Instagram. Wallaahi (by Allaah), it truly is not a necessity. The shaytaan comes to us and says: «Something interesting may happen, and something beautiful may be shared». The messages that reach you via Facebook, via everything and anything: with 90% you take in a bad influence, and you may take in 10% good influence. And the definition of Islaam: «Warding off harms takes precedence over bringing about benefits». That is why it is important that people give up Facebook. And if you think that you will need an account one day, then keep your account but do not oblige yourself to go to it. If you want to share something, share it and leave. Do not go looking at the likes and how it was spread, and so on, otherwise you will let your heart become occupied with that afterwards. This you must not do. These fitan (trials) are better avoided despite the good you see in them. Facebook must be given up. In this era you also have another form of sending messages, so make sure you are not hunched over it. Read what is important and leave. Set notification tones for the important groups. The ustaadh is in very many groups. He has turned off the sound of all groups. He turned off, to begin with, [the notification] from all people. So when a message comes, he does not see it and does not hear it, except for certain matters and certain groups that [are] extremely important and relate directly to the work he is doing; for these he has set certain tones. Each group has a tone, one group or two groups by which you know that something has entered that group. And from certain people he has tones.
When he has rest time, he looks at whether [the matter] is important or not. And when there is no rest time, he does not look and leaves these messages until the rest time. If you do not correct [the matter] in this way and organise it, you will not be able to live and your life will become the smartphone. It is not possible to restrain yourself from this fitnah except by organising yourself strictly in a way in which you are moderate: you do not go to excess so that you are no longer available at all — for the responsibilities you must fulfil — and your life does not become the smartphone. When you want to read something or write it or look it up, then do not do that on the smartphone, is the advice of the ustaadh. Do that on the computer. Go to the computer, for that is better than receiving all these things on your smartphone. It only takes one app coming in, and you are immediately distracted at that moment, thereby wasting a lot of time without knowing it. If you were to add [it] up, you may have sat two or three hours behind the smartphone, and then you ask yourself: what did I do, how many hasanaat did I earn, what supposedly useful information [did I obtain]? Zero.
Many people say [that] many beautiful things are shared via Facebook. These beautiful things you can also obtain through other than Facebook, through your brothers and sisters. Through the adhkaar (remembrances of Allaah), the righteous deeds, and ikhlaas. That is better than throwing yourself into a fitnah from which it is very difficult to get out. And among the good advices is also that the pop-up notifications (pop-ups) that you have from every app, you turn off, except from the very important apps (such as WhatsApp). And apart from that you do not need any of the other things, unless you need other things because you have — for example — a certain responsibility.
Perhaps the sisters have other advices, then they can mention them — in shaa Allaah.
A sister turns off all WhatsApp notifications.
Question: How can I motivate my partner to sit on his phone less?
The answer: Motivating the partner towards awareness of time, of wasting time, and of the time one can spend in another way — in talking with his wife, the children, the adhkaar, etc. — that is, that you make him, as much as possible, dislike spending time in this way, and that you — as a woman — try to be interesting to your husband. Adorn yourself, be attractive and interesting to your husband. The matter has two sides. And both sides must be used.
Experience of student 4
The sister focused on the behaviour towards her parents, that is, [that] she does what they want without them asking. She has not arrived yet, but she sees that she has made progress in that. Before, she thought that she does nothing except when it is asked of her. She was, at the same time as her father, about to go out, and they were at breakfast at the same time, and this is something that does not happen often.
She focused on doing what the parents want without them asking her. She thought more about her words and deeds. By sometimes listening to what they say, and sometimes doing what they want her to do. She is making progress.

٢) مُمارَسةُ النقاط التي ناقشناها في الدرس، وللأخوات اللاتي نِلنَ تصحيحًا فيما يتعلّق بواجبهنّ المنزليّ السابق، أن يُمارِسنَه على وجهٍ أحسنَ بحسب التصحيح الذي نِلنَه.

نحن الآنَ بصدد تحسين أنفسنا نحوَ رضا الله سبحانه وتعالى وتَعلُّمِ عاداتٍ معيّنة. وهذه العاداتُ الجديدةُ تحتاج إلى وقت. حين لا نُدَرِّب أنفسنا تَكرارًا فسيَصعُب أن نُلازِم هذه الأمورَ — في النهاية — أيضًا. ولذلك سنُؤدّي واجبنا المنزليَّ على هذا الوجه — إن شاء الله — في الأسابيع القادمة.

الدرس الأربعون — الأحد ٩ ديسمبر ٢٠١٨

الواجب المنزلي (٢ ديسمبر)
sections.content_nl:
Samenvatting van de les van 2 december
Deze week sprak de ustaadh over de communicatie tussen de partners, en over de tarbiyah van de echtgenoot en de echtgenote, en wat daarin de essentiële punten zijn die nodig zijn om het praktisch te beoefenen en erin te volharden.
Het is belangrijk in het huwelijk dat er een goed begrip [is] met betrekking tot de communicatie. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa heeft de verhouding [de relatie] tussen de man en de vrouw uiteengezet. De man moet het gedrag van de vrouw bijsturen overeenkomstig haar positie. In de communicatie [zijn er] essenties die volbracht en verwezenlijkt worden met betrekking tot beide kanten (de man richting de vrouw, en de vrouw richting de man). Deze essenties vormen de communicatie tussen hen beiden.
Wij hebben de vorige les drie essenties behandeld:
De man en de vrouw moeten beiden in hun hoofd, door middel van hun verstand, weten en erkennen dat zij hun taken moeten uitvoeren. En daar moet je ook in je communicatie rekening mee houden.
In de communicatie [moet] de vrouw nederig [zijn] en de positie accepteren die Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa gegeven heeft en aan haar echtgenoot gegeven heeft, en die ook verwezenlijken.
Het uitspreken van de juiste woorden (of de woorden die je gaat uitspreken jou dichter bij Allaah brengen).
De man en de vrouw moeten beiden in hun hoofd, door middel van hun verstand, weten en erkennen dat zij hun taken moeten uitvoeren. En daar moet je ook in je communicatie rekening mee houden.
De man moet opstaan als leider, als opvoeder, en als iemand die beoordeelt volgens de weegschaal van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. De man mag zichzelf niet gelijkstellen aan de vrouw. Hij mag niet — wanneer er van de vrouw bepaalde gedragingen komen — een gelijksoortige reactie teruggeven. Hij moet boven zulk gedrag staan en zulk gedrag rechtzetten. Dat doet hij door eerst zichzelf recht te zetten, geduld te hebben, en het gedrag bij de vrouw te verbeteren. Dit is een verantwoordelijkheid die Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa aan de man heeft gegeven.
En de vrouw — van de andere kant — moet nederig zijn en niet tegen de man rebelleren. En tot wat haar toebehoort, hoort dat zij [het verborgene] bewaart [met wat Allaah bewaard heeft] in wat Allaah bewaakt heeft. Dat wil zeggen [dat zij] niet spreekt over iets wat zich in haar huwelijk heeft afgespeeld, behalve wanneer zij haar recht wil terugkrijgen. En dat [gebeurt] alleen bij iemand [die] kennis [heeft] en betrouwbaar is, die deze zaak niet misbruikt en haar niet doorvertelt aan anderen. Zij mag deze zaak alleen kenbaar maken om haar rechten terug te krijgen, als zij dat niet bij de man kan.
En ook moet de vrouw de man ondersteunen in zijn verantwoordelijkheid, waarover hij op de Dag der Opstanding ondervraagd zal worden. Zij moet hem adviseren, zich nederig tegenover hem opstellen, geduld met hem hebben, zijn leiderschap niet ondermijnen, en zich niet boven hem verheffen, zeker niet in het bijzijn van de kinderen.
Wanneer de vrouw deze taak accepteert en verwezenlijkt, en eveneens de taak van haar echtgenoot accepteert en ondersteunt, dan vormt de relatie hier een belangrijk fundament. En dat geldt ook van de man richting de vrouw. En dit moet ook beoefend worden in hun communicatie.
De nederigheid van de vrouw en haar acceptatie van de positie van de man, waarmee zij Allaah aanbidt.
Dat wil zeggen [dat] de positie van de man — de vrouw moet daarmee Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa aanbidden. Dat betekent dus dat zij dichter tot Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa moet komen door middel van het verwezenlijken van [de rechten van] de man, dat wil zeggen: hoe zij op nederige wijze met haar echtgenoot spreekt. Wij hebben genoemd hoe de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sprak over de vrouw die steeds terugkeert [de 3aoed, de berouwvol terugkerende].
Wanneer de vrouw haar echtgenoot niet tevredenstelt, dan zal Allaah ook niet tevreden zijn over de vrouw, en dat betekent dat de mate van iemaan van de vrouw afhangt van [de mate van] de tevredenheid van de man.
De tweede essentie in de communicatie [is] dus dat de vrouw nederig is en de positie accepteert die Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa gegeven heeft en aan haar echtgenoot gegeven heeft, en dat zij die ook verwezenlijkt.
Het uitspreken van de juiste woorden
Dat wil zeggen [dat] de beide partners, voordat zij hun woorden uiten, zichzelf moeten onderzoeken en zichzelf moeten afvragen of wat zij gaan zeggen hen dichter bij Allaah zal brengen of niet, en niet louter moeten vertrekken vanuit een tegenreactie of wraak door middel van het woord. Vervolgens moeten zij zichzelf afvragen of [de zaak] een schadelijke invloed heeft op de liefde en de relatie. Want wanneer iemand een woord uitspreekt, kan het [zo] zijn dat die [persoon] door middel van één woord een kuil graaft die moeilijk te dichten is en die men nog heel lang blijft herinneren. Zolang het woord niet naar buiten is gekomen, is het jouw gevangene. En wanneer jij het woord uitspreekt, dan ben jij de gevangene van het woord. Het is belangrijk dat je niet de gevangene van je woord wordt en dat je het daarna moet verdedigen of verbeteren. Zorg ervoor dat je je woord verbetert zolang je het nog niet hebt uitgesproken. Zal ik de shaytaan tegen haar helpen, of zal ik haar tegen de shaytaan helpen? Ook de vrouw moet zo over haar echtgenoot denken. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa zal die [persoon] ter verantwoording roepen voor wat hij heeft uitgesproken. En wanneer het woord niet is uitgesproken en in het hoofd is gebleven, dan wordt het niet aangerekend.
En daarom is het belangrijk dat eenieder — de man en de vrouw — de beste woorden uit en eerst zichzelf onderzoekt: waartoe zal [de zaak] leiden, wat is de invloed van mijn woord op de ander? Wanneer iemand zijn woord uitspreekt, is het niet langer jouw gevangene, maar ben jij de gevangene van jouw woord. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa waarschuwt ons voor de shaytaan. Hij maakt ons duidelijk wat de oplossing tegen de shaytaan en de djinn is: dat je zegt «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم» — «Ik zoek toevlucht bij Allaah tegen de vervloekte shaytaan». Wanneer iemand de ander wil adviseren, dat hij begint met de ander te adviseren en de isti3aadhah verricht door tegen hem te zeggen: «Voordat wij verdergaan, zeg: ‹ik zoek toevlucht bij Allaah tegen de vervloekte shaytaan›» of door aayat al-Kursie te reciteren. Deze isti3aadhah is een belangrijke zaak waarmee je jouw communicatie moet beginnen wanneer jij een slechte uitspraak hebt gedaan of een ander een slechte uitspraak heeft gedaan. Vervolgens zegt Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa dat Hij As-Samie3 (de Alhorende) is over wat wij doen en zeggen, en dat Hij Al-3Aliem (de Alwetende) is over onze harten, dat wil zeggen: over de intenties waarmee wij dat uitspreken. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa maakt in deze verzen duidelijk welk medicijn je kunt gebruiken, wat de oorsprong van dat medicijn is, en wat de methode van het medicijn is.
Voordat je spreekt is het belangrijk dat je de tevredenheid van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [als doel] vaststelt. Je moet geduld hebben met wat je zegt en het beste zeggen. De oorsprong van het medicijn bij het goede spreken [is] het geduld, en het medicijn zelf bij het spreken [is] dat je de beste uitspraken hebt. En om zo'n medicijn op de juiste wijze in te nemen, moet je de isti3aadhah verrichten. En zelfs al zou je geen influisteringen [hebben], dan moet je de isti3aadhah verrichten om de influisteringen af te weren.
En een voorbeeld hiervan is dat je tegen jouw echtgenoot zegt: «Moge Allaah tevreden over jou zijn, moge Allaah over jou waken, ik wil jou heel graag tevredenstellen, ik wil dat Allaah ons beschermt». Wij hebben eerder uiteengezet dat de goede communicatie inhoudt dat men naar de ander luistert, zich openstelt, communiceert zonder oordeel. Dat was toen wij het accepteren van het advies (de nasiehah) behandelden. Daarna behandelden wij ook het geven van het advies. Het accepteren van het advies moet gepaard gaan met een zuivere intentie bij het luisteren. En tot de belangrijke zaken hierin behoort dat wij die les nog een keer lezen en proberen die te verwezenlijken.
Bij het luisteren is het heel belangrijk dat je jezelf bewust maakt van de positie waarin jij je bevindt en waarmee je moet luisteren; want het luisteren heeft betrekking op de positie waarmee je luistert: ben jij een leerling of een leraar? Ben jij iemand met gezag of iemand boven wie gezag staat? Ben jij degene die leidt of degene die geleid wordt? Beide maken verschil in het luisteren.
Het probleem van veel mannen en vrouwen is dat zij luisteren vanuit een onjuiste positie. En het is belangrijk dat jullie vanuit een juiste positie naar elkaar luisteren. Bij de beide partners geldt dat zij moeten luisteren volgens de taak die Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa voor hen heeft bestemd.
En de vrouw moet dus luisteren vanuit haar positie als een nederige, volgzame vrouw, die opgevoed wordt, die van haar echtgenoot moet leren, of [die] naar oplossingen zoekt, of [die] zoekt hoe zij haar echtgenoot tevreden kan stellen, hoe zij haar echtgenoot kan aanvullen, hoe zij zijn leiderschap kan ondersteunen en er niet tegenin kan gaan. Vanuit deze taak en deze positie moet de vrouw luisteren, en ook al wordt haar onrecht aangedaan, dan moet zij hem adviseren vanuit haar positie. Zij zorgt ervoor dat zij het hart van haar echtgenoot wint en spreekt vervolgens goede woorden. En dat behoort tot de belangrijke zaken die ook horen bij het afweren van het slechte met het betere. Dat je ook nadenkt: vanuit welke positie moet ik luisteren, en hoe moet ik mijn echtgenoot op de juiste wijze beïnvloeden?
De positie van de man en de vrouw past ook bij onze fitrah (natuurlijke aanleg). Je moet vanuit die positie luisteren en spreken.
Hoe weet je op welke wijze iemand naar jou geluisterd heeft? Dat kun je — meestal — ook zien aan hoe hij gesproken heeft. Wanneer hij met het oor van een leraar heeft geluisterd, dan zal hij als een leraar spreken. Wanneer de vrouw luistert vanuit de positie [dat] zij het voor het zeggen heeft [de overhand heeft], dan zal dat ook duidelijk zijn uit haar woorden en de wijze waarop zij haar woorden plaatst en haar houding aanneemt terwijl zij spreekt.
Het luisteren heeft ook invloed op de reactie [het weerwoord].
Bij sommigen is de fitrah gebroken, waarbij de positie van de ander wordt ingenomen. Wanneer dat gebeurt, zullen er conflicten ontstaan.
sections.title_nl: De communicatie en de tarbiyah tussen de echtgenoten
sections.content_en:
Summary of the lesson of 2 December
This week the ustaadh spoke about the communication between the partners, and about the tarbiyah of the husband and the wife, and what the essential points are that are needed in this so that we can practise it practically and persevere in it.
It is important in marriage that there be a good understanding with regard to communication. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has clarified the relation [the relationship] between the man and the woman. The man must adjust the behaviour of the woman according to her position. In communication [there are] essentials that are accomplished and realised with regard to both sides (the man towards the woman, and the woman towards the man). These essentials form the communication between the two of them.
We dealt with three essentials last lesson:
The man and the woman must both know in their heads, by means of their intellects, and acknowledge that they must carry out their tasks. And you must also take that into account in your communication.
In communication, [that] the woman [be] humble and accept the position that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given and has given to her husband, and also realise it.
Uttering the right words (whether the words you are going to utter bring you closer to Allaah).
The man and the woman must both know in their heads, by means of their intellects, and acknowledge that they must carry out their tasks. And you must also take that into account in your communication.
The man must stand up as a leader, an educator, and one who assesses according to the scale of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. The man must not equate himself with the woman. He must not — when certain behaviours come from the woman — return an equal reaction. He must be above such behaviour and must correct such behaviour. He does that by first correcting himself, being patient, and improving the behaviour in the woman. This is a responsibility that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given to the man.
And the woman — from the other side — must be humble and not rebel against the man. And part of what belongs to her is that she preserves [the unseen] [with what Allaah has preserved] in what Allaah has guarded. That is [that she] does not speak about something that took place in her marriage except when she wants to reclaim her right. And that [happens] only with someone [who has] knowledge and is trustworthy, who does not misuse this matter and does not pass it on to others. She may only disclose this matter in order to reclaim her rights if she cannot do so with the man.
And the woman must also support the man in his responsibility, about which he will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. She must advise him, be humble with him, be patient with him, not undermine his leadership, and not exalt herself above him, especially not in the presence of the children.
When the woman accepts this task and realises it, and likewise accepts her husband's task and supports it, then the relationship here forms an important foundation. And that also applies from the man towards the woman. And this must also be practised in their communication.
The humility of the woman and her acceptance of the position of the man, with which she worships Allaah.
That is [that] the position of the man — the woman must worship Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa through it. So that means that she must draw closer to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa by means of fulfilling [the rights of] the man, that is: how she speaks with her husband in a humble manner. We mentioned how the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam spoke about the woman who keeps returning [al-3aoed, the one who returns repentantly].
When the woman does not please her husband, then Allaah will also not be pleased with the woman, and that means that the degree of the woman's iemaan depends on [the extent of] the man's pleasure.
The second essential in communication [is] therefore that the woman is humble and accepts the position that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given and has given to her husband, and that she also realises it.
Uttering the right words
That is [that] the two partners, before they express their words, must examine themselves and ask themselves whether what they are going to say will bring them closer to Allaah or not, and not proceed purely from a counter-reaction or revenge by means of the word. Then they must ask themselves whether [the matter] has a harmful effect on the love and the relationship. For when someone utters a word, it can be [the case] that that [person], by means of one word, digs a pit that is difficult to fill and that one keeps remembering for a very long time. As long as the word has not come out, it is your prisoner. And when you utter the word, you are the prisoner of the word. It is important that you do not become the prisoner of your word and then have to defend it or improve it afterwards. Make sure that you improve your word as long as you have not uttered it. Will I help the shaytaan against her, or will I help her against the shaytaan? The woman must also think about her husband in this way. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will hold that [person] to account for what he has uttered. And when the word has not been uttered and has remained in the head, then it is not held against him.
And that is why it is important that everyone — the man and the woman — delivers the best speech and first examines himself: where will [the matter] lead, what is the effect of my word on the other? When someone utters his word, it is no longer your prisoner, but you are the prisoner of your word. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa warns us against the shaytaan. He makes clear to us what the solution against the shaytaan and the djinn is: that you say «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم» — «I seek refuge with Allaah from the accursed shaytaan». When someone wants to advise the other, that he begins by advising the other and performs the isti3aadhah by saying to him: «Before we continue, say: ‹I seek refuge with Allaah from the accursed shaytaan›» or by reciting aayat al-Kursie. This isti3aadhah is an important matter with which you must begin your communication when you have made a bad utterance or another has made a bad utterance. Then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says that He is As-Samie3 (the All-Hearing) over what we do and say, and that He is Al-3Aliem (the All-Knowing) of our hearts, that is: of the intentions with which we utter that. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa makes clear in these verses which medicine you can use, what the origin of that medicine is, and what the method of the medicine is.
Before you speak, it is important that you set the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [as a goal]. You must be patient with what you say and say the best. The origin of the medicine in good speech [is] patience, and the medicine itself when speaking [is] that you have the best utterances. And in order to swallow such a medicine in the correct manner, you must perform the isti3aadhah. And even if you had no whisperings, you must perform the isti3aadhah in order to repel the whisperings.
And an example of this is that you say to your husband: «May Allaah be pleased with you, may Allaah watch over you, I very much want to please you, I want Allaah to guard us». We have explained before that good communication entails that one listens to the other, opens up, communicates without judgement. That was when we dealt with accepting advice (the nasiehah). Then we also dealt with giving advice. Accepting advice must be paired with a sincere intention when listening. And among the important matters in this is that we read that lesson once more and try to realise it.
When listening, it is very important that you make yourself aware of the position you are in and with which you must listen; because listening relates to the position with which you listen: are you a pupil or a teacher? Are you someone with authority or someone over whom there is authority? Are you the one who leads or the one who is led? Both make a difference in listening.
The problem of many men and women is that they listen from an incorrect position. And it is important that you listen to one another from a correct position. With the two partners, they must listen according to the task that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has designated for them.
And the woman must therefore listen from her position as a humble, compliant woman, who is being educated, who must learn from her husband, or [who] seeks solutions, or [who] seeks how she can please her husband, how she can complete her husband, how she can support his leadership and not oppose it. From this task and this position the woman must listen, and even if injustice is done to her, she must advise him from her position. She makes sure that she wins her husband's heart and then utters good words. And that is among the important matters that also belong to repelling the evil with the better. That you also think: from which position should I listen, and how should I influence my husband in the correct manner?
The position of the man and the woman also suits our fitrah (natural disposition). You must listen and speak from that position.
How do you know in what manner someone has listened to you? You can — usually — also see that from how he spoke. When he has listened with the ear of a teacher, he will speak as a teacher. When the woman listens from the position [that] she has the say [the upper hand], then that will also be clear from her words and the manner in which she places her words and assumes her posture while she speaks.
Listening also has an effect on the response [the reaction].
In some people the fitrah is broken, whereby the position of the other is taken. When that happens, conflicts will arise.
