«Ik heb nog relatief veel begeerten, en dat betekent dat mijn iemaan niet voldoende is, want de ustaadh zei dat er óf iemaan aanwezig is, óf begeerte. Hoe minder iemaan, hoe meer begeerte. En hoe minder begeerte, hoe meer iemaan.
Ik moet mijn iemaan verbeteren voor mijzelf, en ook voor het moment waarop ik — in shaa Allaah — een opvoedster zal zijn. Ik moet mij meer bezighouden met de istighfaar, en de adhkaar van de ochtend en de avond met grotere regelmaat verrichten, en ik wil — in shaa Allaah — in plaats van mijn tijd te besteden aan zaken die geen nut hebben (zoals sociale media; Facebook) boeken lezen over de Eigenschappen van Allaah en Zijn Schone Namen met de uitleg ervan, en over de engelen. Ik moet mij bewuster zijn van de Laatste Dag en dat aanwezig laten zijn in mijn daden.
En bovendien heb ik mij deze afgelopen week beziggehouden met het advies van de ustaadh met betrekking tot sociale media, met name Facebook. Ik heb het van mijn telefoon gewist. Subhaana-llaah (verheven is Allaah), ik was werkelijk verslaafd aan mijn telefoon/Facebook. Soms is [het] nog steeds moeilijk voor mij dat Facebook niet meer op mijn telefoon staat. Ik probeer mij te focussen op andere, belangrijkere zaken, maar ik merk dat het mij werkelijk moeite kost — subhaana-llaah.
Alleen daarmee heb ik mij beziggehouden, omdat ik dit heel belangrijk vind, en het een grote invloed heeft op mijn leven en mijn tijd.
Het verbeteren van het gedrag
Wat betreft mijn gedrag denk ik dat [het] eerst begint met het bewustzijn, en het vermeerderen van kennis over hoe de mens in elkaar zit, om mijzelf daarmee te wapenen. Wij hebben in de eerste fase de beïnvloedingsfactoren van de mens behandeld. Ik zie dat het goed voor mij is om die stof af en toe te herhalen. Daarnaast is er zeker een verbetering die bereikt moet worden in mijn gedrag, in mijn denken, en in mijn hart, en in mijn daden.
Ik merk dat ik alles wat met gedrag te maken heeft interessant vind. Ik wil niet leren op basis van de westerse psychologie, omdat ik verkeerd beïnvloed zou kunnen worden. Zijn er islamitische boeken die de ustaadh kan aanraden om meer te leren over het gedrag op islamitische wijze, zoals het inzicht in de eigenschappen van de mens?»
De ustaadh: Het nadenken over de eigenschappen van de mens. Dit kun je heel gemakkelijk leren uit de Qur-aan en de Sunnah. Wanneer je in de verzen van de Qur-aan zoekt naar «de mens» of «de mensen» of «zoon van Aadam» of «kinderen van Aadam», dan zul je daar ongetwijfeld één of meer eigenschappen van de mens vanuit zijn fitrah vinden. En precies hetzelfde geldt voor de Sunnah. Deze zaak heeft Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa ons in de Qur-aan gegeven. En wie weet hoe hij deze zaken moet aansturen op de wijze die wij ook geleerd hebben, die zal veel succes hebben in zijn leven. En wat jij op dat moment moet doen, is jezelf beter leren kennen. Je moet vooral letten op de fundamentele wijze van aansturing [sturing]. En de fundamentele wijze van aansturing is gebouwd op de eigenschappen van de mens, namelijk dat hij van het goede houdt en het slechte verafschuwt. Als jij deze eigenschap kent en weet dat de bron van het goede en het slechte niets anders is dan de Qur-aan en de Sunnah, dan weet je ook hoe je de zaak aanstuurt, zoals de nieuwsgierigheid, en het haasten naar het resultaat, en de vergeetachtigheid, en dergelijke. Wij moeten ervoor waken dat wij dingen leuk gaan vinden omdat ze interessant lijken. Dat is de eigenschap van de nieuwsgierigheid. Je moet de eigenschap zo aansturen dat jij van het goede houdt en het slechte verafschuwt. Je moet alleen nieuwsgierigheid hebben naar wat jou baat in het tevredenstellen van Allaah, zodat je haar op die wijze inzet. En dat je alles verafschuwt wat Allaah vertoornt. Dat je daar niet meer in geïnteresseerd bent. En zo kun je jouw prioriteiten op betere wijze aansturen en ordenen. Wanneer jij jouw nieuwsgierigheid ordent, en jouw prioriteiten vaststelt in het tevredenstellen van Allaah, dat wil zeggen de kennis van Tawhied, maak daar dan een bezigheid van. En de minder belangrijke zaken, zoals de zaken die te maken hebben met de media, en hoe er met de media gemanipuleerd wordt, of dat men kennis verzamelt omdat hij dat interessant vindt. Men vindt het interessant om kennis te verzamelen over hoe mensen aangestuurd worden en hoe zij aangestuurd worden. Stuur eerst jezelf aan met Tawhied.
«Hiervan kan ik veel leren. Ik merk dat ik het enigszins moeilijk vind om de middenweg te nemen. Ik ben meestal in een toestand van ‹alles of niets›, en ik verval in de laksheid (het niet doen van wat Allaah bevolen heeft) of in de overdrijving (het doen van wat Allaah niet bevolen heeft). En ook hier zie ik dat het bewustzijn hiervan de eerste stap is. En uiteindelijk is het belangrijk dat ik mijzelf blijf afvragen of ik mijn zaken verricht volgens de tevredenheid van Allaah. Ik wil de overdrijving in mijn tarbiyah of de laksheid daarin vermijden. Door het verbeteren van de eerste drie definities (de iemaan, het volgen van de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, het verbeteren van mijn gedrag) zal ik de middenweg volgen — in shaa Allaah. Voorbeeld: elke vrijdag lees ik per se met mijn echtgenoot de Qur-aan...».
De ustaadh: Als ik weet dat mijn echtgenoot op dat moment niet kan, dan kan ik doorgaan met de zaak. Het wordt overdrijving wanneer ik ruzie krijg met mijn echtgenoot [over het feit] dat het per se [zo] moet omdat het in het schema staat. De afspraak is een afspraak. Wij hebben dit in het schema staan. Je mag hem eraan herinneren, en hem adviseren, maar het schema blijft een richtlijn [leidraad]. Het evenwicht hierin is uiterst belangrijk. Het afwegen moet gebeuren met de weegschaal van de tevredenheid van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. Wanneer wij dit als maatstaf nemen, dan zullen wij niet laks zijn en niet overdrijven. Als jouw echtgenoot niet aanwezig is, dan verlies je misschien wat motivatie. En de laksheid is dat je de Qur-aan helemaal niet reciteert.
Ervaring van studente 5
De zuster dacht dat wij geen huiswerk hadden. Zij is doorgegaan met het werken aan de communicatie op de wijze die wij geleerd hebben.
De ustaadh: Wij moeten dit huiswerk niet behandelen als huiswerk, maar als levenswerk. Wat wij nu doen is een belangrijke stap voor onze komende tijd, om onszelf te verbeteren. Je hebt die impuls nodig om jezelf daadwerkelijk te trainen.
Wat heb je te delen wat betreft de communicatie?
De zuster: Voordat zij iets zegt, is zij zich bewust van haar woorden. Wanneer zij naar de regels kijkt, heeft zij ze doorgenomen. En zij vindt het nog steeds moeilijk om om te gaan met wat zij als onrecht ervaart, of het aandringen, of het langdurig doorgaan over een bepaald onderwerp, waardoor zij er niet op reageert en niet op de juiste wijze reageert.
De ustaadh: Wat heb je verbeterd? Wat heb je daadwerkelijk goed gedaan?
De zuster: Haar moeder vroeg haar of zij haar vader ergens over wilde raadplegen. Zij dacht na over de beste wijze daarvoor. De zuster is tevreden over hoe de zaak is verlopen. Haar vader was in zijn slaapkamer. Zij mocht binnenkomen nadat zij had geklopt. Zij zag dat hij blij was om haar te zien. Zij heeft daarvan gebruikgemaakt op de wijze van de vader-dochterrelatie. Zij vroeg op vriendelijke wijze waarover haar moeder hem wilde raadplegen. Zij heeft geleerd dat men niet direct ter zake moet komen, maar met een verzachtende aanpak te werk moet gaan. Het handelen volgens die positie. Zij vond dat een goed leermoment.
sections.title_nl: De definities van de tarbiyah
sections.content_en:
The most important thing you should know about tarbiyah is that tarbiyah has definitions and guidelines that serve as scales and foundations upon which tarbiyah is built. And in order to actually carry out tarbiyah in the correct way, be steadfast in it, and make it succeed, it is important that we know these definitions (the definitions of tarbiyah).
Without these definitions tarbiyah will not succeed; indeed, if we were to base tarbiyah on other definitions, tarbiyah would fail. It is important that we know these definitions, and that we know how we can practise them in order to implement them correctly.
Iemaan
Iemaan is the first and most important definition upon which tarbiyah is built, and it is a definition with which we also improve our tarbiyah (our deeds), and with which we also improve the deeds of the one we educate. It is not possible to realise a tarbiyah (upbringing) without iemaan. The definition of iemaan is the definition from which you also proceed to improve all other matters, of deeds and sayings.
Iemaan is in the heart. So when it improves and is corrected, it will in the end also yield its fruits in that the deeds change and the sayings change. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also makes that clear: «ألم تَرَ كيف ضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمةً طَيِّبةً كشَجَرةٍ طَيِّبةٍ أَصلُها ثابِتٌ وفَرعُها في السماء، تُؤتي أُكُلَها كلَّ حِينٍ بإذنِ رَبِّها» — Interpretation of the meaning: «Do you not see how Allaah presents a parable: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky. It gives its fruit at all times, by the permission of its Lord.» (Soerat Ibraahiem, verses 24-25). What does that mean?
That means, then, that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa here compares the good word (laa ilaaha illallaah — there is no god worthy of worship except Allaah) to a good tree, a sound, healthy tree. The healthy tree has roots rooted in the earth; from these roots grows a tree trunk, and on this trunk grow branches, and from them come fruits. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says here about this tree that its root is firm. And here Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa compares the roots to the deeds of the heart. When the deeds of the heart (iemaan) have a firm establishment in the heart, the limbs will act on that basis. And when iemaan roots itself firmly in the heart, the deeds afterwards act [in accordance with it].
And conversely, that means that when there is no iemaan, there are no deeds [either]. And when iemaan is shaken in the heart, the righteous deeds are shaken with it, and there is no firm establishment of the deeds.
And with regard to tarbiyah, we must work on iemaan.
Tarbiyah has three pillars:
The murabbie (educator)
The murabbaa (the one being educated)
The content of the tarbiyah and its method
All three pillars must be connected to the foundation of iemaan. For when one of these three pillars is not built on iemaan, there is a deficiency, and tarbiyah cannot be realised in the correct way. The murabbie himself must have iemaan.
That is why it is important that the murabbie occupies himself with istighfaar, performing the obligatory deeds, and then performing the voluntary deeds he is able to, in order to increase his iemaan.
That is: also increasing istighfaar alongside his obligatory deeds, and the adhkaar of the morning and the evening, so that his iemaan remains in continuous flow and his iemaan is renewed. And that is extremely important.
When [iemaan] is not present, tarbiyah does not proceed in the correct way, and the tarbiyah acquires another scale, and the tarbiyah fails. The decisions the murabbie takes are then not built on iemaan, but on desire. The less iemaan, the more desire. And the less desire, the more iemaan. So: either iemaan, or desire. And this is something the father and the mother must pay attention to, and the teacher (male and female) must also pay attention to when they impart [knowledge] to people and educate people. That is an extremely important matter.
That is why it is important that the murabbie occupies himself as much as possible with iemaan, such as gathering knowledge, increasing voluntary deeds alongside his obligatory deeds, and increasing the admonitions that soften his heart — and those admonitions you can also read in many ahaadieth, many verses, and stories in the Qur-aan and the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition) and from reality; they soften your heart and give you a greater boost of iemaan — and the right environment, and the right people around you who remind you of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
The knowledge you gather as a murabbie must be general Islamic knowledge, but also knowledge specific to the tarbiyah you are carrying out, and the iemaan connected to it. So you must know which issues of iemaan are the ones upon which what I now want to address in my tarbiyah is built. All issues of iemaan are connected to one of the six pillars of iemaan or to several of them. So the murabbie himself must constantly improve his iemaan, increase it and keep it renewed.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «الإيمانُ أن تُؤمِنَ بالله، وملائكتِه، وكتبِه، ورسلِه، واليومِ الآخر، والقَدَر، خيرِه وشَرِّه» — «Iemaan is that you believe in Allaah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its evil.»
In all your life you must live by these six pillars. When you live by these six pillars and live these pillars with all their details, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will give you more iemaan in your heart.
Iemaan in Allaah: getting to know more about the Names of Allaah and His Attributes, and the actions of Allaah, and the signs Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has created in His creation, which prove His knowledge, His power, His strength, His wisdom and all His beautiful, exalted attributes.
Then you get to know His legislations more. Iemaan in the angels: what kinds of angels are there, how do they deal with us and how should we deal with the angels. When you know this world, your iemaan grows exceedingly. For example, that some angels are entrusted with the wind, and with the rain, and others entrusted with thunder, and others entrusted with guarding over you, and others writing down your deeds, on the right and on the left.
And others stand behind you in the salaah. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says that when a person on his journey (the man) performs the adhaan (call to prayer) and then the iqaamah (announcement of the start of the prayer), behind him pray of the angels as far as his sight reaches. For example, if a person is praying and reciting in his prayer, then the one [of the angels] standing behind him [receives the recitation], to the point that he places his mouth upon his mouth, and he catches every word of his recitation so that it does not fall to the ground. And part of that is that the angel of the right says, for example, to the angel of the left: do not write this down, wait six hours, he may repent. So the angel of the right is the leader of the angel of the left.
When we grasp the world of the angels, we reach an extremely lofty iemaan. And likewise with the Books. That we believe in the Books, in all the Books that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has sent down: the scriptures of Ibraahiem, the Indjiel (the Gospel), the Tawraat (the Torah), and the Qur-aan. That Allaah sent down His word to mankind. And that you read the stories of the messengers, and that you live them. In them you learn how Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa deals with the people who obey Him and those who do not obey Him.
The Last Day: when you go and read it and live it, magnificent. From the moment one dies until he remains in Paradise or the Fire. And in the divine decree you learn how to deal with good and evil events. If you have the foundation of iemaan, you will be able, with iemaan, to educate another. And if you do not have this foundation, you will fail in all these matters by not investing life for the sake of Allaah. You will see the angels as a secondary matter, without us knowing that there are angels who guard over us, pray behind us, or take the Qur-aan from our mouth. Without us knowing that Allaah created angels. Until the Day of Resurrection they will prostrate and remain prostrating. And yet Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will show His delight in the one who rises in the middle of the night, performs wudoe' (ritual ablution), and performs a few raka3aat (units of prayer) for Him. Allaah will say: look at this servant, this one has prostrated to Me. Magnificent that there are angels who commend us so that [Allaah] listens to us.
If you do not occupy yourself with that, you will focus only on what is tangible, on the worldly.
If you do not believe in the Books, your iemaan is much less, and you will occupy yourself purely with the evil of the disbelievers. Even though you remember that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent down Books to them as well.
If you do not have these matters, you will act in another way and educate in another way.
And also the lack of awareness of the Last Day: then you will not deal with your deeds consciously, and you will not weigh your deeds with the scale of the Last Day. Then you will say: what will people say.
And whoever does not occupy himself with iemaan in the divine decree will have many frustrations, to the point that he may even reach depression.
That is why it is important that the first pillar (the murabbie) occupies himself with iemaan.
The second pillar is the murabbaa. And the first thing that must be planted is iemaan. When you plant something else, you are at that moment building on quicksand. And when you build on quicksand, that building will not last. The first thing you teach him is iemaan. You acquaint him with all these matters we have just dealt with, and why Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa commanded him that, and why this [was] the best for him, and that it will constitute success in this world and the hereafter. The first thing you must work on with the murabbaa is iemaan, by means of the content we have just dealt with.
And the content, the third pillar, is the content we have just dealt with: gathering knowledge, performing the obligatory deeds, performing the voluntary deeds, etc.
3Aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa (may Allaah be pleased with her) was the most knowledgeable among the wives of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and among all the women of the sahaabah (companions). She said: «Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent down of the Qur-aan in Makkah the soewar of al-mufassal (which are the last chapters of the Qur-aan), and they [spoke] about Paradise and the Fire, and about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, that is, they were about iemaan. Then when the people entered Islaam (and that was after the hidjrah — emigration — of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam), after thirteen years, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent down the halaal (permissible) and the haraam (forbidden). What does that mean? 3Aa-ishah clarifies: if in Makkah at the beginning it had been sent down ‹do not drink wine›, there would have been people saying: we will never leave wine; and ‹do not commit zinaa (fornication)›, the people would have said: we will never leave zinaa. But in Makkah it was sent down: ‹when I was a little girl it was sent down: nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter›. Soerat Al-Baqarah and Soerat An-Nisaa-e were only sent down when I was with him, in Al-Madienah. And in them are many legislations of the legislations of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa». So you see that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa takes into account this human being whom He created with his natural disposition, so He first sends down of the Qur-aan what reaches his heart in order to open his heart, and then sends down what is halaal and what is haraam. And that is the main method with which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa raised the sahaabah. First iemaan, then the rulings (the halaal and the haraam). The scholars say: «First comes the iemaan by which one comes to life, then come the rulings when the legislations come that give people guidelines», and that is like the bow and the arrow. This arrow you draw back firmly in the bow. Then you aim at the target, and that is tarbiyah. Tarbiyah must consist of these two levels.
Iemaan — what does iemaan do to the heart? It gives life to the heart.
What do the legislations, in which there is: this is halaal and this is haraam, do? They give direction to the matter.
You need both matters, iemaan together with direction. And they are inseparable from one another.
When there is only iemaan, that is, life, without direction, dangerous situations will arise; you do not know which way one should head, but he has great energy. That is why it is important that these two matters exist: iemaan and direction. And you must begin with iemaan, because without iemaan the heart accepts nothing.
That is why [it was that] the first verses Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent down during thirteen years spoke only about Tawhied (the Attributes of Allaah and His Names, the signs of Allaah).
When the sahaabah had been raised with them, then they gave everything for the sake of this Islaam, and then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sent down the legislations of the halaal and the haraam.
This [is] the comparison with the bow and the arrow. The arrow you draw back in the bow, thereby forming energy. Then you must go and aim; if you aim and release the arrow, it sets off in the direction of the right target. If you have no energy, that is, no iemaan, but [you have] direction, nothing will happen. And when you have iemaan and no direction, you may inflict harm on others without knowing it.
This [is] the system of iemaan with which we must educate. That we first give the one we want to educate iemaan, then give him direction. This is the main method upon which tarbiyah is built, and which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa used and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam used.
«من كان يُؤمِنُ بالله واليومِ الآخر، فلْيُكرِم ضَيفَه» — «Whoever believes in Allaah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest.» First he addresses the heart, then he says: this you must do. And in many verses and many ahaadieth, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa clarifies in the verses what the factors of success are, and what the reward is, and when Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa clarifies the forbidden matters, He also clarifies by means of the warning of the punishment.
Question: I wondered how we can — in the best way — learn about the angels. Are [there] reliable books on that?
The answer: The ustaadh will look for that and try to put [the book] or its title in the app [the WhatsApp group].
Following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam
In tarbiyah, it is important that the three pillars of tarbiyah also adhere to following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (the murabbie, the murabbaa, and the method of tarbiyah). Among the matters that should be clarified is that we must follow the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And the evidences for this are numerous in the Qur-aan. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says, for example: «يا أيُّها الذينَ آمَنوا اسْتَجِيبوا للهِ وللرَّسولِ إذا دَعاكُم لِما يُحييكُم واعْلَموا أنَّ اللهَ يَحُولُ بينَ المَرءِ وقَلبِه» — Interpretation of the meaning: «O you who believe, respond to Allaah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allaah intervenes between a man and his heart.» (Soerat Al-Anfaal, verse 24). So that means that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa commands the believers to respond to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and to the Messenger sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and thereby their iemaan will also grow. And thus you see that following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (the second definition) is a completion of the first definition.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «فلمَّا زاغوا أَزاغَ اللهُ قُلوبَهم واللهُ لا يَهدي القَومَ الفاسِقين» — Interpretation of the meaning: «So when they deviated, Allaah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allaah does not guide the gravely sinning people.» (Soerat As-Saff, verse 5). Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says thereby that when people deviate from following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will cause their hearts to deviate. And it is important that we know that following the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also nourishes the first definition of the definitions of tarbiyah (iemaan). In addition to the verses that also clarify to us that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa commands us to follow the Messenger sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «وما آتاكُمُ الرَّسولُ فخُذوهُ وما نَهاكُم عنه فانْتَهوا» — Interpretation of the meaning: «And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.» (Soerat Al-Hashr, verse 7).
And [there are] many other verses commanding us to take the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam as an example.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «إذا أَمَرتُكم بأمرٍ فأْتوا منه ما استَطَعتُم، وإذا نَهَيتُكم عن شيءٍ فاجتَنِبوه» — «When I command you with a matter, then do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you something, then avoid it.»
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam came to increase our iemaan, and to teach us to hold fast to the Sunnah of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and to give us guidelines on how to educate. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam came as a murabbie. And there is no doubt that he was also given a method with which he educates.
The murabbie, the murabbaa, and the tarbiyah itself must all adhere to this foundation, namely following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
And this must also be a guiding light in the communication with the murabbaa. The murabbie must clarify: «We will do this because the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam commanded us to», or «We will leave this because the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam forbade us from it», and in order to increase our iemaan.
Improving behaviour
The third foundation is improving behaviour. The murabbie, the murabbaa, and the tarbiyah itself must all adhere to improving behaviour.
That means that the one who educates must improve his behaviour. First he must examine his behaviour in a good way; then it is important that he also takes into account that tarbiyah revolves around improving the behaviour of the one he educates. And that also means that he must do everything to improve that behaviour, starting with safeguarding that [person's] sight, hearing, heart and thoughts, so that that [person] also behaves correctly himself. The content of the tarbiyah must be about improving behaviour, according to the priorities. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also sent His Messenger Muhammad sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam for this. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «هو الذي بَعَثَ في الأُمِّيِّينَ رسولًا منهم يَتلو عليهم آياتِه ويُزَكِّيهم» — Interpretation of the meaning: «He is the One Who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses and purifying them.» The tazkiyah (purification) is the improvement intended here. The improvement in thinking, heart and deeds. And this was the way in which the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam dealt with the sahaabah.
Whenever he saw that the sahaabah should improve [themselves], the behaviour, he said something about it. But he approached each person in a fitting way, in a way that suited him. The one who had knowledge he approached in a different way from the one who was ignorant. And the one who was young he approached in a different way from the one who was a wise elder; the young man he approached in a different way from the child, and so on. The goal, and also one of the foundations, [is] improving the thinking, the heart and the limbs.
Wasatiyyah (following the middle course)
Another important foundation in tarbiyah is wasatiyyah (moderation).
Wasatiyyah means the middle path. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «وكذلك جَعَلناكُم أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لتكونوا شُهَداءَ على الناسِ ويكونَ الرَّسولُ عليكم شَهيدًا» — Interpretation of the meaning: «And thus We have made you a middle nation, so that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you.» (Soerat Al-Baqarah, verse 143).
Wasatiyyah also means the best and the most elevated.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «كنتُم خَيرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخرِجَتْ للناسِ تأمُرونَ بالمَعروفِ وتَنهَونَ عن المُنكَرِ وتُؤمِنونَ بالله» — Interpretation of the meaning: «You are the best nation brought forth for mankind: you enjoin the good and forbid the evil and you believe in Allaah.» (Soerat Aal 3Imraan, verse 110).
So that means that it belongs to the foundations of our religion that we are a middle nation that follows a moderate methodology.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa clarifies here why we are the best nation. Why we are a middle nation: we enjoin the good, and forbid the evil, and that leads us to iemaan in Allaah. Not only that, but also because we stand between the laxity of [the Christians] and the excess of [the Jews]. The laxity of the Christians and the excess of the Jews. And we have also received rules and legislations far milder than the legislations of the Jews and the Christians. How is wasatiyyah realised in tarbiyah?
The murabbie himself must be a moderate person. He must be someone who neither goes to excess nor is lax, but carries out his affairs and carries out his tarbiyah according to the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. When he is someone who goes to excess, he will also go to excess in his tarbiyah. And when he is someone who does not adhere precisely to the legislations of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, he will also educate in that manner.
And the same: he will follow an incorrect methodology. Thus the Khawaaridj (a deviant sect) raise their children in a manner of excess, and the Soefies raise their children in a manner of laxity.
Excess is doing what Allaah did not command you. And laxity is leaving what Allaah commanded you. And wasatiyyah leads to steadfastness in tarbiyah. The murabbie will not find [the matter] burdensome in tarbiyah, and the murabbaa will not find [the matter] burdensome in tarbiyah. So one holds on to what he is raised upon, for wasatiyyah leads to steadfastness.
If you go back to the first definition (iemaan), you see that the foundation of iemaan — when it is built on following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and when its content is improving behaviour — then that will show through wasatiyyah.
This wasatiyyah is also realised only by means of the fifth definition.
Taking the priorities into account
Taking the priorities into account means that you do not want to solve everything at once when it cannot be combined together, but you look at the priorities Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has determined. And with that you begin. And that is only possible when the murabbie applies his tarbiyah within himself, then gives it to the murabbaa, and also maintains it in the tarbiyah.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, when he sent Mu3aadh ibn Djabal to Yemen, said to him: «إنَّك ستأتي قومًا من أهلِ الكتاب. فإذا قَدِمتَ عليهم، فادْعُهم إلى شهادةِ أن لا إلهَ إلَّا الله وأنَّ محمَّدًا رسولُ الله. فإن أَطاعوكَ لذلك، فأَخبِرهم أنَّ اللهَ افتَرَضَ عليهم خمسَ صلواتٍ في كلِّ يومٍ وليلة» — «You will come to a people of the People of the Book. So when you arrive to them, call them to the testimony that there is no god worthy of worship except Allaah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allaah. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allaah has obligated upon them five prayers in every day and night.»
So that means that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam laid out for Mu3aadh a plan with priorities, for after that [there are] also other matters the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam placed in steps, among them the zakaah (obligatory alms). And thereby the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam clarifies that when they do not obey you in «laa ilaaha illallaah», it is not permissible to move on to the salaah, and when they do not obey you in the salaah, it is not permissible to move on to the zakaah.
Those are important, determined priorities in the da3wah (calling to Allaah). And without taking the priorities into account, tarbiyah will not be realised. Many situations and many matters become corrupted, so that you do not know where to begin. So it is important that you hold fast to the priorities. These priorities are extremely important, because with them you will also be able to realise wasatiyyah.
You begin with Tawhied, then you move on to the salaah. And when [the matter concerns] a woman, you move on to the hidjaab (Islamic covering). And exactly the same applies here as well between the man and the woman. When the man wants to educate his wife, it is important that he begins at the beginning, Tawhied (the goal of life), then moves on from it, then improving the salaah, then we look at the hidjaab, whether there is something that needs improvement. Then we move on to less important matters.
When you take the priority into account, you will be able to realise your tarbiyah in a gradual manner.
Tasfiyah (purification)
So when you have the iemaan on which you have built your tarbiyah, then the following of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam which also increases the iemaan, then the improvement is realised by means of following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and the iemaan, and you follow in that a moderate path built on the priorities at that moment, then you must also build your tarbiyah on tasfiyah.
What do we mean here by tasfiyah?
Tarbiyah must be built on the pure, unadulterated knowledge with which one educates. And the pure, unadulterated knowledge is built on what Allaah said (qaala Allaah), and what the Prophet said (qaala rasoelu-llaah), and what the sahaabah said. And built on what pleases Allaah. Without knowledge of all the preceding matters, and without this definition, one cannot educate.
Upon every murabbie rests the duty to gather knowledge about the way in which he should educate his wife. That is why he must gather knowledge about the legislation of Allaah, the reward, and the punishment. For part of tarbiyah is admonition.
So that he begins with what the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam began with, and according to his plan in improvement and tarbiyah he also realises the tarbiyah. And thereby you can also realise wasatiyyah.
That is also why the man must strive as much as possible to have more knowledge than his wife concerning Islamic matters. And that is easier for him because he is more flexible in his time, and he disposes over his priorities and the division of his time, so that he can later educate his wife and children with it. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «ولا تَقفُ ما ليس لك به علم» — Interpretation of the meaning: «And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge.» (Soerat Al-Israa-e, verse 36).
Taysier (facilitation)
The murabbie must do the easiest so that his tarbiyah truly succeeds. The murabbie must choose the easiest of that with which he realises his tarbiyah. 3Aa-ishah also says: «ما خُيِّرَ النبيُّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم بين أمرين إلَّا اختار أيسرَهما ما لم يكن إثمًا» — «The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was never given the choice between two matters except that he chose the easier of the two, as long as it was not a sin.»
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says in a hadieth: «أحبُّ الأعمالِ إلى الله أَدوَمُها وإنْ قَلَّ» — «The most beloved deeds to Allaah are the most constant of them, even if they are few.» And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «خذوا من الأعمالِ ما تُطيقون، فإنَّ اللهَ لا يَمَلُّ حتى تَمَلُّوا» — «Take on of the deeds what you are able to bear, for Allaah does not grow weary until you grow weary.» Taysier is an important foundation in tarbiyah. And this will also prolong the steadfastness of the tarbiyah and its continuity.
Shumuliyyah (comprehensiveness)
The murabbie must educate with a comprehensive system, and not address only one issue, or point at one issue without looking at the comprehensiveness of the issue. And shumuliyyah also means that one searches for the roots of the issue and begins there with the improvement and the tarbiyah, and does not look only at the symptoms, the manifestations and the branches, for that is the methodology of the disbelievers which, unfortunately, many Muslims follow. That they occupy themselves only with outward behaviour, appearance, and symptoms, and not with the original roots that are the causes of the behaviour, such as the thinking or the deeds of the heart. When these begin to improve, the limbs will follow. That is the comprehensiveness of the issue.
And part of the comprehensiveness of the issue is that the matter is improved from all its sides. Bad behaviour is connected to incorrect thinking, incorrect feelings, incorrect habits, an incorrect environment, and incorrect impulses and promptings. One must look at all these things, not only at the environment or the outward behaviour or improving the person in himself without looking at the friends (male and female). No, one must look at the whole.
And part of shumuliyyah is also that every issue is directly connected to 3aqiedah (creed) (to the way in which one believes). As the ustaadh said just now: down to the roots. That is why it is important that you get to know the one you educate well, so that you know his environment, and what he does, and what goes on in his heart, and what he is influenced by, and where his weak points lie, and where he sets himself against. All these things you must know about the one you educate. That is why the man must know all these things about his wife, so that he can improve these things in his wife, and so that he knows how his wife is influenced.
That is why Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «يا أيُّها الذينَ آمَنوا ادْخُلوا في السِّلْمِ كافَّةً ولا تَتَّبِعوا خُطُواتِ الشيطانِ إنَّه لكم عَدُوٌّ مُبين» — Interpretation of the meaning: «O you who believe, enter into Islaam completely and do not follow the footsteps of the shaytaan. Verily, he is a clear enemy to you.» (Soerat Al-Baqarah, verse 208).
[The matter] begins with us — as educators — also using a comprehensive, complete system ourselves. And that [is] the system of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, which does not occupy itself only with the symptoms but also with the roots and the condition of the one being educated and who influences him at that moment (the murabbaa).
Tawaazun (balance/proportionality)
Balance means that tarbiyah is practised with correct scales so that this tarbiyah has balance, and does not lean too much towards the negative and does not tilt too much towards the positive. Like the method «Tripple P» — a method laid down by the disbelievers. Its content is that one directs the one he educates only towards the positive with an educational programme. You speak to him only with the positive, and you direct him only to the positive, and you build — as they claim — only positive energy with the person you educate. And that is a lax approach. And that is an approach that does not teach the person any boundaries.
And another upbringing is built only on rebuke, accusation and negativity. These are unbalanced systems. The Islamic system is built on balance and moderation. For with moderation you reach stability, moderation, and steadfastness. Where does this balance lie? When one must perform righteous deeds, he is motivated with love. And when he must desist, he is warned of the punishment of Allaah. And both lead to the desire for Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. You flee from Allaah to Allaah. That is: from the punishment of Allaah to the mercy of Allaah. That is the balance that also exists in the 3aqiedah of Islaam.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «إنَّهم كانوا يُسارِعونَ في الخَيراتِ ويَدعونَنا رَغَبًا ورَهَبًا وكانوا لنا خاشِعين» — Interpretation of the meaning: «Verily, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humble before Us.» (Soerat Al-Anbiyaa-e, verse 90).
With that you advance. When you occupy yourself [only] with the fact that you will be punished, that will lead you to nothing except much fear of Allaah, and that is unhealthy and makes one doubt himself a lot or lose motivation. And when one focuses only on the Attributes of Allaah that He is GHafoer (Oft-Forgiving), without remembering that He is severe in punishment, one will not desist from doing evil things.
Question: When should the sisters or the daughters or the granddaughters wear the hidjaab, after the prayer or with the prayer?
The answer: The hidjaab always with the prayer, because among the conditions of the prayer is the hidjaab. Just as among its conditions is the wudoe', so among its conditions is also the hidjaab. From the age of seven.
The next lesson
Next week we will begin the ten steps of tarbiyah.
The homework
Organise your notes by spending at least two hours on them, and read them well once more, and reflect on them.
Look at what you should improve in these nine definitions. Write it down and take the first steps towards improvement. For each definition the ustaadh wants to hear what each one should improve in herself.
The improvement that took place in the past lessons in the points that were about communication also carries over to next week.
Lesson forty-one — Sunday 16 December 2018
The homework (9 December)
Organise your notes by spending at least two hours on them, and read them well once more, and reflect on them.
Look at what you should improve in these nine definitions. Write it down and take the first steps towards improvement. For each definition the ustaadh wants to hear what each one should improve in herself.
The improvement that took place in the past lessons in the points that were about communication also carries over to next week.
This week we will begin the ten steps of tarbiyah.
Discussion of the homework (16 December)
Experience of student 1
The sister occupied herself with the definitions of tarbiyah. She went through all the definitions and noted them down, and noted down points she should work on.
Iemaan: extremely important, because with iemaan you improve everything. Iemaan is the first step because it is connected to all the other steps. She gave herself iemaan as first priority. And what she did in that regard is that she makes sure she follows [the lesson] on time, processes the notes well, and occupies herself with the homework of the lessons.
The ustaadh: There are of course also many other things that can increase iemaan. What you said is correct. And among the important matters connected to increasing iemaan is that one gathers more knowledge about Paradise, and what happens in the hereafter. You need this for yourself, and you also need it when you later go and raise your child, or there is another under your care whom you educate or guide, so that you address him with these rewards or punishments. And among the important ahaadieth in this regard is the hadieth in which the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam relates about his ascension to the seventh heaven, where he meets many people being punished. Then he asks Djibriel (the angel Gabriel) what is happening to them, and for what they are being punished.
And it is important to review this, so that you know which punishment applies to a certain sin, such as eating in Ramadaan, backbiting, going around among people with slander, zinaa, and much more. These things take place in the coming second stage, the stage of the barzakh (the stage in which we are in the grave). These are matters to which we must give great attention.
And also the rewards of the things we perform, and living these rewards.
Following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: this definition is a completion of the first definition, and she lived this, for she occupied herself for the second definition with reading the sierah (biography) of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and she noticed thereby that the love for the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and your iemaan grow strongly, so that you want to apply [the matter] and follow him. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was the best murabbie, and that also reminded her of the incident in which he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sends Anas to do something for him, and something distracts him on the way, and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam smiles. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam had many educational methods, and she found that beautiful.
Improving behaviour: it is the purification of behaviour and the purification of thinking, the heart and the deeds. The sister was very much aware; she thinks about the behaviour she has towards others, and the thinking she has; she reflects on the thinking scheme in order to go through it again and thus purify the thinking.
The ustaadh: A behaviour in which you had to bring about an improvement.
The sister: A specific situation with her mother in which there was not — necessarily — incorrect behaviour, but there was incorrect thinking. There was a situation in which she was annoyed and felt the annoyance. She did not show it, but it was inside her. Then she went through the thinking scheme. The sister awakened her ikhlaas [with the thought] that that annoyance is not correct, and she performed the isti3aadhah, and performed the istighfaar, and then the thinking improved.
The ustaadh: As for the eighth definition, what did you do with it?
The sister: The eighth definition was shumuliyyah, that is, not a superficial improvement but taking all the roots, and improving all sides. The roots are the 3aqiedah, and gathering more knowledge in it. Soon 3aqiedah lessons will start with Aboe Ismaa3iel; she wants to register for them in order to strengthen her roots more.
Experience of student 2
The sister was not present at the last lesson. She read the notes. As for behaviour, she sees that it is extremely important, and she tried, with people within the family who have a high position but who nevertheless say certain things, to show respect by restraining herself.
The ustaadh: More important than that is that one goes deeper into the roots of the problem, namely that one at that moment must have a form of reverence towards the one who is much older than him. And that is what Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also commands us through the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, who says: «ليس مِنَّا من لم يُوَقِّر كبيرَنا» — «He is not of us who does not honour our elder.» That is: he has no reverence from the heart. When reverence is present, it forms a foundation for all the spontaneous behaviours towards the elders. Then you do not need to take the trouble of restraining yourself. Restraining oneself is good, but in the end you should try to make those who are older great in your heart. Then you will feel the inclination to respect them without effort. That is different from finding yourself held back, and needing much patience to restrain yourself.
And among the methods for doing that is that you look at how the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam dealt with the elders: his wet nurse Haliemah, and his disbelieving uncle Aboe Taalib. The sierah teaches us much about how the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam dealt with the elders.
Experience of student 3
The sister occupied herself with the lesson by going through it seriously. Her husband is not present at this time, but she has other family members with whom she can practise the communication. Perhaps [the matter is] the reverse of [the situation of] the [other] sisters. She should be honoured by the family members, but she does not notice that in their behaviour. She tries to be very forgiving, to overlook things, and to give advice. And she also tries to apply it in her work. She is learning not to respond quickly so that a greater blessing descends and she does not give the shaytaan an opportunity.
As for her husband, she tries — when the communication is less — to be understanding about it. And that is what she tries to apply.
The ustaadh: With regard to these definitions (iemaan, following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and the other definitions): they are educational definitions we must also work on within ourselves, and in the tarbiyah we carry out.
Experience of student 4
Iemaan
«I still have relatively many desires, and that means that my iemaan is not sufficient, because the ustaadh said that either iemaan is present or desire. The less iemaan, the more desire. And the less desire, the more iemaan.
I must improve my iemaan for myself, and also for the moment when I will be — in shaa Allaah — an educator. I must occupy myself more with istighfaar, and perform the adhkaar of the morning and the evening with greater regularity, and I want — in shaa Allaah — instead of spending my time on things that have no benefit (like social media; Facebook) to read books about the Attributes of Allaah and His Beautiful Names with their explanation, and about the angels. I must be more aware of the Last Day and make that present in my deeds.
And in addition, this past week I occupied myself with the ustaadh's advice regarding social media, especially Facebook. I deleted it from my phone. Subhaana-llaah (glorified is Allaah), I was truly addicted to my phone/Facebook. Sometimes [it] is still difficult for me that Facebook is no longer on my phone. I try to focus on other, more important things, but I notice that it truly costs me effort — subhaana-llaah.
Only with that did I occupy myself, because I consider this very important, and it has a great effect on my life and my time.
Improving behaviour
As for my behaviour, I think [the matter] begins first with awareness, and increasing knowledge about how the human being is constituted, in order to arm myself with that. We dealt in the first stage with the factors of influence on the human being. I see that it is good for me to repeat that material from time to time. Then there is certainly an improvement that must be achieved in my behaviour, in my thinking, and in my heart, and in my deeds.
I notice that I find everything related to behaviour interesting. I do not want to learn on the basis of Western psychology because I might be influenced wrongly. Are there Islamic books the ustaadh can recommend for me to learn more about behaviour in an Islamic way, such as insight into the attributes of the human being?»
The ustaadh: Reflecting on the attributes of the human being. This you can learn very easily from the Qur-aan and the Sunnah. When you search in the verses of the Qur-aan for «the human being» or «the people» or «son of Aadam» or «children of Aadam», you will without doubt find there one or more attributes of the human being from his fitrah. And exactly the same in the Sunnah. This matter Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given us in the Qur-aan. And whoever knows how to manage these matters in the way we have also learned will succeed greatly in his life. And what you should do at that moment is get to know yourself more. You should pay attention especially to the fundamental way of management [direction]. And the fundamental way of management is built on the attributes of the human being, namely that he loves good and hates evil. So if you know this attribute and know that the source of good and evil is nothing but the Qur-aan and the Sunnah, then you also know how to manage the matter, such as curiosity, and rushing to the result, and forgetfulness, and so on. We must beware of coming to like things because they seem interesting. That is the attribute of curiosity. You must manage the attribute in such a way that you love good and hate evil. You should have curiosity only about what benefits you in pleasing Allaah, so that you activate it in that way. And that you hate everything that angers Allaah. That you are no longer interested in it. And in this way you can manage and organise your priorities in a better way. When you organise your curiosity, and set your priorities in pleasing Allaah, that is, the knowledge of Tawhied, then make that an occupation. And the less important matters, such as the matters relating to the media, and how the media are manipulated, or that one gathers knowledge because he finds that interesting. One finds it interesting to gather knowledge about how people are managed and how they are directed. First manage yourself with Tawhied.
«From this I can learn a lot. I notice that I find it somewhat difficult to take the middle path. I am mostly in a state of ‹all or nothing›, and I fall into laxity (not doing what Allaah commanded) or into excess (doing what Allaah did not command). And here too I see that awareness of this is the first step. And in the end it is important that I keep asking myself whether I am carrying out my affairs according to the pleasure of Allaah. I want to avoid excess in my tarbiyah or laxity in it. By improving the first three definitions (iemaan, following the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, improving my behaviour) I will follow the middle path — in shaa Allaah. Example: every Friday, without fail, I read the Qur-aan with my husband...».
The ustaadh: If I know that my husband cannot at that moment, then I can proceed with the matter. It becomes excess when I enter into a quarrel with my husband [over the fact] that it must necessarily [be so] because it is in the schedule. The agreement is an agreement. We have this in the schedule. You may remind him, and advise him, but the schedule remains a guideline [an indication]. The balancing in this is extremely important. The balancing must take place with the scale of the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. When we take this as a scale, we will not be lax and will not go to excess. If your husband is not present, you may lose some motivation. And laxity is not reciting the Qur-aan at all.
Experience of student 5
The sister thought that we had no homework. She continued working on the communication in the way we have learned.
The ustaadh: We should not treat this homework as homework, but as life's work. What we are doing now is an important step for our coming time, to improve ourselves. You need that push to truly train yourself.
What do you have to share concerning the communication?
The sister: Before she says something, she is aware of her words. When she looks at the rules, she has gone through them. And she still finds it difficult to deal with what she perceives as injustice, or the insisting, or the prolonged continuing on a certain subject, so that she does not respond to it and does not respond correctly.
The ustaadh: What did you improve? What did you actually do well?
The sister: Her mother asked her whether she wanted to consult her father about something. So she thought about the best way to do that. The sister is satisfied with how the matter went. Her father was in his bedroom. She was allowed to enter after she had knocked. She saw that he was happy to see her. She made use of that in the manner of the father-daughter relationship. She asked in a kind way what her mother wanted to consult him about. She learned that one should not go straight to the heart of the matter, but should work with a softening approach. Acting according to that position. She found that a good learning moment.

chapters.title_nl: De definities van de tarbiyah

chapters.title: ٣) النُّطقُ بالكلماتِ الصحيحة

sections.content:
أي [أنَّ] الشريكَين قبل أن يُبدِيا كلماتهما ينبغي أن يَتفقَّدا أنفسهما ويَسألا أنفسهما هل ما سيقولانه سيُقَرِّبهما إلى الله أم لا، لا أن يَنطَلِقا مَحضًا من رَدِّ فِعلٍ مُضادٍّ أو انتقامٍ بواسطةِ الكلمة. ثمَّ ينبغي أن يَسألا أنفسهما هل [للأمر] تأثيرٌ ضارٌّ على المحبَّةِ والعلاقة. فحين يَنطِق المرءُ بكلمةٍ، يمكن أن يكون [الأمرُ] أنَّ ذلك [الشخصَ] بواسطةِ كلمةٍ يَحفُر حُفرةً يَصعُبُ رَدمُها ويَبقى المرءُ يَتذكَّرها طويلًا جدًّا. ما دامت الكلمةُ لم تَخرُج، فهي سَجينُك. وحين تَنطِق بالكلمةِ فأنت سَجينُ الكلمة. من المهمِّ ألَّا تَصير سَجينَ كلمتك وأن يَلزَمَك بعد ذلك أن تُدافِعَ عنها أو تُحَسِّنَها. احرِص على أن تُحَسِّنَ كلمتك ما دُمتَ لم تَنطِق بها. هل سأُعينُ الشيطانَ ضِدَّها، أم سأُعينها ضِدَّ الشيطان؟ ينبغي للمرأةِ أيضًا أن تُفَكِّرَ في زوجها هكذا. اللهُ سبحانه وتعالى سيُحاسِبُ ذلك [الشخصَ] على ما نَطَق به. وحين لا تكون الكلمةُ قد نُطِق بها وبَقِيَت في الرأس، فلا يُعاتَبُ عليها.

ولذلك من المهمِّ أن كلَّ أحدٍ — الرجلَ والمرأةَ — يُؤدِّي أحسنَ الكلامِ ويَتفقَّد نفسَه أوَّلًا: إلى مَ سيقود [الأمرُ]، ما تأثيرُ كلمتي على الآخر؟ حين يَنطِق المرءُ بكلمتِه فلا تَعُود سَجينَتَك بل أنت سَجينُ كلمتك. اللهُ سبحانه وتعالى يُحَذِّرنا من الشيطان. يُبَيِّنُ لنا ما حَلُّ الشيطانِ والجِنّ: أن تقول «أعوذُ بالله من الشيطانِ الرجيم». حين يُريد أحدٌ أن يَنصَحَ الآخرَ، أن يَبدأ بأن يَنصَحَ الآخرَ ويُؤَدِّيَ الاستِعاذةَ بأن يقولَ له: «قبل أن نَمضي، قُل ‹أعوذُ بالله من الشيطانِ الرجيم›» أو بأن يَتلُوَ آيةَ الكُرسيِّ. هذه الاستِعاذةُ أمرٌ مهمٌّ ينبغي أن تَبدَأ به تواصُلَك حيث تكون أنت قد أَدلَيتَ بنُطقٍ سَيِّئٍ أو يكون آخرُ قد أَدلى بنُطقٍ سَيِّئ. ثمَّ يقول اللهُ سبحانه وتعالى إنَّه السميعُ على ما نَفعَلُ ونقول، وإنَّه العليمُ بقلوبنا، أي بالنيَّاتِ التي نَنطِق بها بذلك. اللهُ سبحانه وتعالى يُبَيِّنُ في هذه الآيات أيَّ دَواءٍ تستطيع أن تَستعمِل، وما أصلُ ذلك الدواء، وما طريقةُ الدواء.

قبل أن تَتكلَّم من المهمِّ أن تُحَدِّدَ رضا الله سبحانه وتعالى [هَدَفًا]. ينبغي أن تَصبِر على ما تقول وأن تقول الأحسن. أصلُ الدواءِ في النُّطقِ الحَسَنِ [هو] الصبر، والدواءُ نفسُه عند النُّطقِ [هو] أن تكون عندك أحسنُ الأنطاق. ولأن تَتجرَّعَ مثلَ هذا الدواءِ على الوجه الصحيح، ينبغي أن تُؤَدِّيَ الاستِعاذة. ولو لم تَكُن [عندك] وَساوس، ينبغي أن تُؤَدِّيَ الاستِعاذةَ لتَدفَع الوَساوس.

ومثالٌ على هذا أن تقولَ لزوجك: «رَضِيَ اللهُ عنك، رَعاكَ اللهُ، أريد جدًّا أن أُرضِيَك، أريد أن يَحرُسَنا الله». بيَّنَّا من قبلُ أنَّ التواصلَ الحَسَنَ مَضمونُه أنَّ المرءَ يَستمِع إلى الآخر، يَنفتِح، يَتواصَل بلا حُكم. ذلك كان حين تناولنا قَبولَ النصيحة (النَّصيحة). ثمَّ تناولنا أيضًا إعطاءَ النصيحة. قَبولُ النصيحة ينبغي أن يَقتَرِنَ بنيَّةٍ خالصةٍ عند الاستِماع. ومن الأمورِ المهمَّةِ في هذا أن نَقرأَ ذلك الدرسَ مرَّةً أخرى ونُحاوِلَ أن نُحَقِّقَه.

عند الاستِماع من المهمِّ جدًّا أن تَجعَلَ نفسَك واعيًا بالموقعِ الذي أنت فيه والذي ينبغي أن تَستمِعَ به؛ لأنَّ الاستِماعَ له صلةٌ بالموقعِ الذي تَستمِع به: هل أنت تلميذٌ أم مُعَلِّم؟ هل أنت صاحبُ سلطانٍ أم من تحته سلطان؟ هل أنت من يَقود أم من يُقاد؟ كلاهما يَفرِق في الاستِماع.

مُشكِلةُ كثيرٍ من الرجالِ والنساءِ أنَّهم يَستمِعون من موقعٍ غيرِ صحيح. ومن المهمِّ أن تَستمِعَ من موقعٍ صحيحٍ بعضُكما إلى بعض. عند الشريكَين ينبغي أن يَستمِعا بحسبِ المهمَّةِ التي خصَّصها لهما اللهُ سبحانه وتعالى.

والمرأةُ ينبغي إذًا أن تَستمِعَ من موقعها بوصفها امرأةً مُتواضِعةً، مُنقادة، تُربَّى، ينبغي أن تَتعلَّمَ من زوجها، أو [التي] تَلتمِسُ حلولًا، أو [التي] تَلتمِسُ كيف تستطيع أن تُرضِيَ زوجها، كيف تستطيع أن تُكَمِّلَ زوجَها، كيف تستطيع أن تَدعَمَ قيادته ولا تُعارِضها. من هذه المهمَّةِ وهذا الموقعِ ينبغي أن تَستمِعَ المرأةُ، ورغم أنَّه يُلحَقُ بها ظُلمٌ ينبغي أن تَنصَحَه من موقعها. تَحرِص على أن تَكسِبَ قلبَ زوجها ثمَّ تَنطِق بكلماتٍ حسنة. وذلك من الأمورِ المهمَّةِ التي تَنتمي أيضًا إلى دفعِ السيِّئِ بالأحسن. أن تُفَكِّر أيضًا: بأيِّ موقعٍ ينبغي أن أَستمِع، وكيف ينبغي أن أُؤَثِّر في زوجي على الوجه الصحيح؟

موقعُ الرجلِ والمرأةِ يُناسِبُ أيضًا فِطرتَنا (الاستِعدادَ الطبيعيَّ). ينبغي أن تَستمِعَ وتَتحدَّثَ من ذلك الموقع.

كيف تَعلَم على أيِّ وجهٍ استمَع إليك أحد؟ ذلك تَستطيع — في الغالب — أن تَراه أيضًا من كيف تَكلَّم. حين يكون قد استمَع بأُذنِ مُعَلِّم، فإنَّه سيتحدَّث مُعَلِّمًا. حين تَستمِعُ المرأةُ من موقعِ [أنَّ] لها الكلامَ [اليدَ العُليا]، فإنَّ ذلك سيكون واضحًا أيضًا من كلماتها والوجهِ الذي تَضَع به كلماتها وتَضَع به هَيئتها وهي تتحدَّث.

الاستِماعُ له تأثيرٌ أيضًا على الاستِجابة [رَدِّ الفِعل].

عند بعضهم الفِطرةُ مَكسورة، حيث يُؤخَذ موقعُ الآخر. حين يحدث ذلك ستَنشَأ نِزاعات.
تَتِمَّة
sections.content_nl:
Vervolg
Wij zullen de praktische stappen van de tarbiyah bespreken, dat wil zeggen het traject van de tarbiyah.
Wanneer wij in ons hoofd een uiterst duidelijke voorstelling hebben van het traject van de tarbiyah, en een duidelijk beeld van de weg die wij moeten bewandelen voor de tarbiyah, en wij ook weten waarom wij deze weg moeten bewandelen, dan wordt het gemakkelijker voor ons om deze tarbiyah te verwezenlijken, en zullen wij deze tarbiyah ook met precisie kunnen verwezenlijken, omdat wij ook weten welke stappen wij moeten volgen wat betreft de volgorde van deze stappen, en wat betreft de situatie waarin wij ons bevinden. Want elke situatie heeft haar eigen stappen en haar eigen prioriteiten. En daarmee kun je minder fouten maken, omdat je jezelf ook kunt controleren aan de hand van bepaalde stappen, en je zult veel tijd besparen wat betreft het traject van de tarbiyah. Want als jij de juiste volgorde en de juiste stappen hebt, dan zul je veel tijd besparen in plaats van in veel chaos terecht te komen en niet te weten waar je moet beginnen.
sections.title_nl: De communicatie en de tarbiyah tussen de echtgenoten
sections.content_en:
Continuation
We will discuss the practical steps of tarbiyah, that is, the course of tarbiyah.
When we have in our heads an extremely clear conception of the course of tarbiyah, and a clear picture of the path we should walk for tarbiyah, and we also know why we should walk this path, it becomes easier for us to realise this tarbiyah, and we will also be able to realise this tarbiyah with precision, because we also know which steps we should follow in terms of the order of these steps, and in terms of the situation we are in. For every situation has its own steps and its own priorities. And thereby you can make fewer mistakes, because you can also monitor yourself according to certain steps, and you will save a lot of time with regard to the course of tarbiyah. For if you have the right order and the right steps, you will save a lot of time instead of entering into much chaos and not knowing where to begin.
